rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes an annealing treatment to enhance interfacial short-range order, whereas the paper varied the modulation period (λ) during deposition to create different interface types (coherent, semicoherent, grain-boundary-dominated). This is a different kind of intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses sustained loading at a constant creep-activating temperature, while the paper used room-temperature nanoindentation creep with varying loading rates and a 100 s hold. These are different regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes enhanced interfacial short-range order leading to dislocation trapping and pile-up-driven creep. The paper's mechanism involves semicoherent interfaces blocking dislocations, causing pile-up and stress-induced interfacial amorphization that enables atomic diffusion or interface slip. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher creep rate in annealed samples. The paper found that the semicoherent (λ=16 nm) sample had the highest creep resistance and a transition to diffusion/interface-slip creep, which is the opposite direction of effect.
